notes:
Summary: Sagebrook is a fast-growing SaaS support platform evaluating a hosted RAG stack for customer KB search. Primary focus is embeddings + lightweight neural reranking to push precision for short queries. Index scale target: 1.5M-2.5M KB articles (avg 300-700 tokens). QPS target: 800-1,200 steady-state during peak; spikes to 2k+. Cost sensitivity: finance wants net cost per successful query <= $0.002 (embedding + ANN + rerank).

Key technical preferences / asks:
- Prefer Redwood hosted API initially (speed to market); evaluate Dedicated later if unit cost or isolation needed.
- Reranker: small cross-encoder for top-20 candidates, latency budget for rerank <= 80ms.
- ANN: looking at HNSW vs IVF-PQ tradeoffs, want recommended recall/latency profiles for their 2M index.
- Embedding model: open-model preference (cost) but willing to eval Redwood curated models for throughput/quantization.

Quote from CTO on 2026-02-18 call: "We need reliable 99th pctl latency under load — if you can demo consistent 95ms median and clear cost math, procurement moves fast."

POC notes & results so far:
- Ingest pipeline: incremental delta updates + metadata tags for product/region.
- Initial pilot (250k docs) shows median latencies: embed 12ms, ANN lookup 18ms, rerank 74ms (single-reranker instance).
- Bottleneck: CPU of reranker at 1k QPS; SE suspects batching and quantized model variant can lower cost and latency.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Detailed cost breakdown for per-query with batching at 1k QPS and expected savings with prefix caching.
- Recommended index config for 2M docs where P99 < 300ms and recall > 92% for top-10.
- SLAs and log retention options (30/90/365 days) and exportability for audit.

Next steps agreed: 72h scale test on hosted API (staging keys), Redwood to provide reference cost projection and index config suggestions. SE to submit test plan by 2026-03-09.
